I was working on the rigs and the break away cable on the doghouse trailer was broken off. My push wanted me to drive it anyways. I refused. We got in a yelling match and I said I quit and this was my two week notice. He said fine, went to town and bought a new brake switch and installed it. He insists now that he will drive it even though I'd drive it now that it was fixed. I worked my two weeks and went home, planning on taking a month or two off. The next day I got a call from my old derrick hand. He heard I quit and recruited me to go work on his rig that he was now drilling on. It was still for the same company. If he had just swallowed a bit of his pride I would have stuck around.

Edit: as requested

Break away cable: attaches from a trailer to the tow vehicle. If the trailer somehow becomes disconnected from the truck, the trailer breaks will activate, stopping/slowing the trailer.

Doghouse trailer: a trailer towed by a large truck. The rigs electrical generator, parts and tools are stored in it. It also has a lunch/change room area in half of it.

Push: the rigs manager. He's the head guy on site in charge of the actual rig. He has a boss on site, the consultant. He's is the oil companies representative.

Drive it is just driving the truck towing the trailer

Derrick hand: the guy who has to go up the Derrick of the rig whe. Running pipe in and out of the hole. He is also responsible for running the rigs pump. There are generally 5 guys who work on a service rig. The push, the driller, the derrick hand, and two floor hands.

Since the topic was recently brought up in this subverse I thought I'd list out some practices that I've used over the years to help hone my intuition a bit. In my experience, a sharp "inner eye" is one of the most essential tools for a magician. Many of the features in the spells and rituals I do arise from an intuitive hunch that I should do something a specific way, or at a specific place, or with a specific individual. I don't really know how or why it works, but these are some things I've done to practice and hone it:

  • Sort a deck of playing cards by color (and later by suit) without looking at it.
  • Sit somewhere and visualize what the area looked like 50,100, 500, 10,000, etc years ago.
  • "Follow" walls and hallways with my awareness to "see" what is there
  • "Observe" the plant inside a seed
  • Practice finding things with dowsing rods
  • Decide I want to see something then let my feet lead the way to it (I live in a city so I might decide, for instance, I want to see a bright red bicycle then walk in the direction I feel I'll find it)
  • Guess the number, letter, etc when I play with number and letter generators
  • Alternately, guess the card or call the dice before it's drawn/tossed.
  • Decide who texted me before I look at my phone after I get a text

It's interesting you bring this topic up. I was talking to @pagantree the other day about just this issue, but I didn't know what word to call it. I was bemoaning my lack of "intuition" (psychic awareness, precognition, magical-ness, what have you) and how being able to do things like astral projection, visualize auras, practice witchcraft, etc. are impossible for me because I have little in the way of what is needed to make those things possible. For example, he shuffles a deck of Tarot and (when focusing on the same question) pulls the same or very similar cards each time, no matter how many times he reshuffles and draws. I get new cards each and every time :P. I have plenty of other examples of how I just don't seem to have the "knack" for actually enacting change through rituals and spells.

Anyway, he mentioned the inner eye (brow chakra) as being important for perceiving energies and such not readily available in the mundane world. Not that spending time learning how to open and close the chakras would be a waste of time, as it's valuable in and of itself, but do you think it would help with being able to participate more fully in magickal practices, in developing "intuition"?

I don't know. I don't use chakras. I do classical energy work and I've noticed that it seems to pool differently in certain parts of the body but that's all I know on the subject.

I've developed my intuition simply by using it. The tradition of witchcraft I trained in doesn't see much difference between "psychic awareness" and "awareness" ie there's nothing mystical or special about it. The former merely refers to a level of awareness that other people don't typically reach. Much of our awareness building activities center around observing the self and the others, and also studying perception and the ways it can be manipulated. We drew heavily from Rudolf Steiner's work in these regards, and also the topic of deep ecology. It's pretty dry stuff compared to all the flashy poetry and psychic teas and crystal clusterfucks found in a lot of "witchcraft handbooks" in the new age section, but it gets the results.

Re: the tarot deck, have you tried working with different decks? Sometimes people don't jive with specific decks. I have a deck someone gave me that just refuses to read no matter how I try it. Beautiful deck, but we just don't get along.
